  tampered : single.payload.json with one byte changed in identity.docker-reference

  nonstrict: single.sig.b64 with a newline inserted after byte 20

## fixed check order
  1 key: one PEM 'PUBLIC KEY' block, no trailing data, <= 4 KiB, PKIX, *ecdsa.PublicKey on P-256   -> ErrMalformedKey | ErrUnsupportedKey
  2 signature: every byte in the base64 alphabet, then StdEncoding.Strict()                         -> ErrMalformedSignature
  3 ecdsa.VerifyASN1(key, SHA-256(exact payload bytes), DER sig), payload <= 64 KiB                -> ErrBadSignature
  4 only now parse the payload JSON                                                                -> ErrMalformedPayload
  5 critical.type == 'cosign container image signature'                                            -> ErrWrongPayloadType
  6 critical.image.docker-manifest-digest == the resolved digest                                    -> ErrDigestMismatch
  identity.docker-reference is returned, never checked (cosign payloads are not repository-bound).

## decisions
- wrong key vs tampered payload: the SAME class (ErrBadSignature), distinct only as fixtures. ECDSA verification yields one bit;
  a wrong key and a modified payload are indistinguishable to the verifier, and a message that claimed to tell them apart would
  be guessing. The product can still say which key it tried (the SPKI fingerprint) so an operator can tell the cases apart.
- a valid signature over another digest is ErrDigestMismatch, never ErrBadSignature (TestDigestMismatchIsNotInvalidSignature).
- malformed key and non-P-256 key are distinct classes (ErrMalformedKey vs ErrUnsupportedKey); P-384 and Ed25519 both refuse.
- a valid signature over a payload of the wrong type is its own class (ErrWrongPayloadType), checked after authentication.
- encoding/base64's Strict() still skips 
 and 
 (TestStdlibStrictStillSkipsNewlines); 'strict base64' needs the explicit
  alphabet pre-check, or a signature annotation with line breaks would verify.

## the verifier (scratch; verify.go)
// Package verify is the B494 row (l) offline cosign verifier: stdlib only
// (crypto/ecdsa, crypto/sha256, crypto/x509, encoding/pem, encoding/base64,
// encoding/json). Scratch code that answers the spike question; it is not the
// product verifier.
package verify

import (
	"bytes"
	"crypto/ecdsa"
	"crypto/elliptic"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"crypto/x509"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"encoding/pem"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
)

// The error classes. Each failure wraps exactly one of these; callers compare
// with errors.Is.
var (
	ErrMalformedKey       = errors.New("malformed public key")
	ErrUnsupportedKey     = errors.New("unsupported public key: want ECDSA P-256")
	ErrMalformedSignature = errors.New("malformed signature encoding")
	ErrBadSignature       = errors.New("signature does not verify over the payload")
	ErrMalformedPayload   = errors.New("malformed simple-signing payload")
	ErrWrongPayloadType   = errors.New("payload is not a cosign container image signature")
	ErrDigestMismatch     = errors.New("payload signs a different manifest digest")
)

const (
	maxKey     = 4 << 10
	maxPayload = 64 << 10
	cosignType = "cosign container image signature"
)

// ParseKey accepts exactly one PEM "PUBLIC KEY" block holding a PKIX ECDSA
// P-256 key, and nothing after it.
func ParseKey(pemBytes []byte) (*ecdsa.PublicKey, error) {
	if len(pemBytes) > maxKey {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d bytes exceeds %d", ErrMalformedKey, len(pemBytes), maxKey)
	}
	blk, rest := pem.Decode(pemBytes)
	if blk == nil || blk.Type != "PUBLIC KEY" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: no PEM PUBLIC KEY block", ErrMalformedKey)
	}
	if len(bytes.TrimSpace(rest)) != 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: trailing data after the PEM block", ErrMalformedKey)
	}
	k, err := x509.ParsePKIXPublicKey(blk.Bytes)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrMalformedKey, err)
	}
	ec, ok := k.(*ecdsa.PublicKey)
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: got %T", ErrUnsupportedKey, k)
	}
	if ec.Curve != elliptic.P256() {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: curve %s", ErrUnsupportedKey, ec.Curve.Params().Name)
	}
	return ec, nil
}

// decodeSig is strict base64 with no whitespace at all: Go's
// base64.StdEncoding.Strict() still skips \r and \n, so they are refused first.
func decodeSig(b64 string) ([]byte, error) {
	for i := 0; i < len(b64); i++ {
		c := b64[i]
		if !(c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z' || c >= 'a' && c <= 'z' || c >= '0' && c <= '9' || c == '+' || c == '/' || c == '=') {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: byte 0x%02x at %d is outside the base64 alphabet", ErrMalformedSignature, c, i)
		}
	}
	sig, err := base64.StdEncoding.Strict().DecodeString(b64)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrMalformedSignature, err)
	}
	return sig, nil
}

// Verify checks, in this fixed order: (1) the key parses as PKIX P-256,
// (2) the signature is strict base64, (3) the DER ECDSA signature verifies
// over SHA-256 of the exact payload bytes, (4) only then is the payload
// parsed, (5) critical.type is the cosign image type, (6)
// critical.image.docker-manifest-digest equals want. The payload is never
// parsed before it is authenticated. identity.docker-reference is returned
// but not checked (cosign payloads are not repository-bound).
func Verify(keyPEM, payload []byte, sigB64, want string) (ref string, err error) {
	key, err := ParseKey(keyPEM)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	sig, err := decodeSig(sigB64)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if len(payload) > maxPayload {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %d bytes exceeds %d", ErrMalformedPayload, len(payload), maxPayload)
	}
	sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
	if !ecdsa.VerifyASN1(key, sum[:], sig) {
		return "", ErrBadSignature
	}
	var p struct {
		Critical struct {
			Identity struct {
				DockerReference string `json:"docker-reference"`
			} `json:"identity"`
			Image struct {
				DockerManifestDigest string `json:"docker-manifest-digest"`
			} `json:"image"`
			Type string `json:"type"`
		} `json:"critical"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &p); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrMalformedPayload, err)
	}
	if p.Critical.Type != cosignType {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %q", ErrWrongPayloadType, p.Critical.Type)
	}
	if p.Critical.Image.DockerManifestDigest != want {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: payload names %s, resolved %s", ErrDigestMismatch, p.Critical.Image.DockerManifestDigest, want)
	}
	return p.Critical.Identity.DockerReference, nil
}
